newsitem.title: UK: London smokers get guide on where to light up.
newsitem.headline: London smokers get guide on where to light up.

text.p: A British smokers' rights group launched on Wednesday what it claimed was the world's first travel guide for smokers.
The 224-page book, "Smoking in London," gives advice to nicotine-loving Londoners on where to find the most smoker-friendly pubs, restaurants, cinemas and even health clubs in the capital.
"There are still a large number of places in London where smokers are welcome," said Marjorie Nicholson, director of Forest, the Freedom Organisation for the Right to Enjoy Smoking Tobacco.
"It is important that people realise that London is not as anti-smoking as some capitals in the world," she told Reuters.
Nicholson claimed that nearly 30 per cent of London residents and workers smoked. This, added to tourists, "means that three million people light up in the capital daily."

The guide lists the medieval door of Westminster Abbey, the cathedral where British monarchs including Queen Elizabeth were crowned, as one of the most "impressive places to light up out of the wind."
"Even better, and quieter, is the doorway of the Abbey Gardens tucked round the back of this famous place of worship," it says.
It also suggests smoking in front of the memorial bust of the late U.S. president John F. Kennedy on Marylebone Road in northwest London.
"London has many historical places to light up," Nicholson said.
